title: Repeated-recording jitter–shimmer covariance fails to improve frozen Parkinson voice prediction in an independent Spanish dataset
abstract: We tested whether within-person covariance of log jitter and log shimmer adds Parkinson case-control information beyond means and marginal variability of five shared acoustic measures. Participant-level models used three recordings per person, trained on 32 Oxford/Colorado subjects and tested unchanged on 80 separately recruited Spanish subjects. Covariance improved discovery leave-one-person-out Brier score by 0.01258, but external Brier worsened from 0.36497 to 0.37525: difference +0.01028 (95% stratified participant-bootstrap interval −0.00394 to +0.02514). External discrimination remained near chance. Penalty and comparator challenges did not establish transfer. Extraction and population shifts, small discovery size and absent shared demographics prevent a biological null conclusion. This is a reproducible negative transport result, not a validated diagnostic biomarker.
